paper.title: Recycling History: Efficient Recommendations from Contextual Dueling Bandits

unmapped: History-constrained duels: the recommended item x_t is chosen from the context set X_t, but the comparison item y_t must be chosen from the user's consumption history H_t = {x_1,...,x_{t-1}}; regret counts only x_t
Context set: fixed number of items drawn i.i.d. each round from a distribution P with ||x|| <= r a.s. and Sigma = E[(x-y)(x-y)^T] positive definite
The learner knows the link function F (smooth, strictly increasing, F(u)+F(-u)=1)
The learner knows (a bound on) lambda_min(Sigma) to set the exploration length tau
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the platform is presented with a set of candidate items $\X_t$ ... each item in $\X_t$ is drawn i.i.d. from a $d$-dimensional distribution $\dist$ ... The platform then picks $\y_t$ from $\H_t$ and asks the user to compare $\x_t$ and $\y_t$. ... $r_t = \util{\x^*_t} - \util{\x_t}$ ... When asked to compare $\x_t$ and $\y_t$, the user picks $\x_t$ with probability $\link(\util{\x_t} - \util{\y_t})$

symbols.lambda_Sigma: minimum eigenvalue of Sigma = E[(x-y)(x-y)^T], x,y iid from the context distribution

conditions: items drawn i.i.d. from P with ||x||_2 <= r a.s. (r is L_feat)
link function F smooth, strictly increasing, F(u)+F(-u)=1, known
holds with probability at least 1 - 3 delta

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ be given. Suppose \algname~ is run with $\tau = O(r^2/{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma)}) \log(d/\delta)$. Then, with probability at least $1 - 3\delta$, \algname~  suffers a cumulative regret of $R_T = O\left(\frac{r}{\kappa\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma)}}d\sqrt{T}\log\left(\frac{T}{d\delta}\right)\right)$ where the $O(\cdot)$ notation hides absolute constants.

results.notes: Regret measured only on recommended item x_t vs per-round best item in X_t. Failure probability is 3 delta. Proof also yields explicit bound 2r tau + alpha*beta*sqrt(2dT log((4r^2 tau + T)/d)) with beta = 8r/sqrt(lambda_min(Sigma)).
